jobs.title: Operations Program Manager - Manufacturing
jobs.description:
Mill is a waste prevention technology company reimagining what it means to eliminate waste, starting with food. We build smart systems and infrastructure for homes, businesses, and municipalities that transform food scraps from landfill-bound waste into valuable resources, including chicken feed. Tens of thousands of Mill’s residential food recyclers are already helping households divert millions of pounds of food scraps every year, paving the way for our upcoming launch of Mill Commercial—the industry’s first end-to-end solution for managing, understanding, and preventing food waste in commercial environments (e.g. grocery, restaurants, food services). At Mill, we are passionate about building easy-to-use, beautifully designed technologies that keep food in the food system and out of landfills.

Role Description:

The Operations Program Manager for Manufacturing will lead the manufacturing expansion execution for Mill Commercial.  We are looking for someone who can manage a fast-paced program with calm and clarity when the pressure is high. This individual will interface both internally and externally, and must be able to represent Mill’s interests clearly and consistently. The OPM is a master communicator, gathering information from vendors, partners, and internal stakeholders and delivering clear and effective messaging to drive decisions.

The Operation Program Manager will be responsible for:

- Managing the startup process of new Manufacturing Partners (MP) for Mill in the Commercial space

- Documentation ownership:

- Master Schedule for factory startup

- MSA (Master Service Agreements) with selected MP

- Aligning with Demand and Planning team on manufacturing ramp and supply capability, including proactive communication of needed lead time for any changes to Plan of Record

- Work with our Global Supply Managers to ensure MP procurement strategy meets Mill's program needs

- Planning key development build activities (DVT, PVT) with engineering team

- Detailed program management for bring-up of MP including development builds and any testing required for certification

Education & Experience

- 10+ years experience in Manufacturing Operations, including direct management  of third parties (CM / JDM / OEM)  for hardware products

- Program management experience in bringing up new manufacturing, either via NPI or (preferred) new manufacturing locations/partners

- Start-up experience desired

- Ability to travel domestically and internationally

The estimated base salary range for this position is $195k to $225k, which does not include the value of benefits or a potential equity grant. A wide range of factors are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets, market conditions, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and business and organizational needs.

jobs.title: Software Applications & Data Program Manager
jobs.description:
Mill is a waste prevention technology company reimagining what it means to eliminate waste, starting with food. We build smart systems and infrastructure for homes, businesses, and municipalities that transform food scraps from landfill-bound waste into valuable resources, including chicken feed. Tens of thousands of Mill’s residential food recyclers are already helping households divert millions of pounds of food scraps every year, paving the way for our upcoming launch of Mill Commercial—the industry’s first end-to-end solution for managing, understanding, and preventing food waste in commercial environments (e.g. grocery, restaurants, food services). At Mill, we are passionate about building easy-to-use, beautifully designed technologies that keep food in the food system and out of landfills.

About the Role
We're looking for a Program Manager to be the air traffic control for the Mill Commercial software platform. This is both a strategic and execution-oriented role: you'll keep multiple software teams (Fleet Management, UI, Data Integrations) moving in sync, make sure resources are deployed against the right priorities, and be the key point of contact for partners and customers whose data integrations are critical to our product.

As requirements and timelines shift, you'll continually re-evaluate priorities and communicate issues or opportunities at the executive level fast. This is a fast-paced, complex organizational role built for a detail-oriented leader who thrives on bringing clarity to ambiguity.

What You'll Do

- Track resourcing across SW teams and applications on the Mill Commercial platform, and flag gaps or conflicts before they become blockers

- Serve as Scrum Master and Jira lead for the SW Applications & Data team

- Own key third-party data integrations, customers, partners, and vendors, including sample data requests, schema, and API connections

- Build and maintain the integrated SW deployment schedule across Fleet Management, UI Design, and Data Integrations

- Run regular executive updates on resourcing, scheduling, and budget

- Turn shifting requirements into a shared set of priorities that eng, product, and partners can plan against

- Surface risks, blockers, and scope creep the moment you see them, with enough context for execs to make a fast call

- Map dependencies across teams (SW, firmware, data, CV) to catch where one team's slip becomes another's blocker

What We're Looking For

- 8+ years of SW program management, with strong preference for SW products with a physical hardware component

- Gen 1 software product experience: you've organized the development of complex, first-generation software products

- Software and firmware knowledge: you've worked with both on-device software and cloud-based applications for monitoring and controlling devices

- Data integration expertise: from native APIs to flat-file ingestion; experience with AI-powered workflows is a plus

- Strong cross-functional executor: you keep eng, product, ops, and sales coordinated, and you run meetings that produce clear decisions and owners

- Technical depth: comfortable in a room full of engineers, you can engage substantively on tradeoffs and know when to escalate

- Shipped multiple software products: you've taken more than one through late-stage development, pilot, and into commercial deployment

- Clear, direct communicator: you write status updates and requirements that get read, not skimmed, and you can distill a messy technical problem into a one-line ask for an exec or a one-page brief for a partner

- Fluent with AI tools: you use AI-powered tools day to day for things like summarizing meetings, drafting requirements or specs, or synthesizing data, and you can help the team find similar leverage in their own workflows

- Advanced with program management tools like Jira, Notion, etc., with experience running Scrum rituals up to and including Scrum of Scrums

- Experience coordinating dependencies across many engineering disciplines, from full stack to computer vision to data integration

The estimated base salary range for this position is $185k to $210k, which does not include the value of benefits or a potential equity grant. A wide range of factors are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets, market conditions, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and business and organizational needs.

jobs.title: Sustaining Program Manager — Consumer
jobs.description:
Mill is a waste prevention technology company reimagining what it means to eliminate waste, starting with food. We build smart systems and infrastructure for homes, businesses, and municipalities that transform food scraps from landfill-bound waste into valuable resources, including chicken feed. Tens of thousands of Mill’s residential food recyclers are already helping households divert millions of pounds of food scraps every year, paving the way for our upcoming launch of Mill Commercial—the industry’s first end-to-end solution for managing, understanding, and preventing food waste in commercial environments (e.g. grocery, restaurants, food services). At Mill, we are passionate about building easy-to-use, beautifully designed technologies that keep food in the food system and out of landfills.

The Role

We are seeking an experienced Sustaining Program Manager to own the day-to-day program management of Mill's Consumer hardware line as it scales from launch into steady-state production. You will take ownership of our sustaining engineering and supply chain activities end to end, driving engineering changes, cost-down and alternate-supply qualification, and daily execution with our contract manufacturers, while keeping engineering, quality, supply chain, retail, legal, and finance partners aligned. You will run our recurring Sustaining Core review, maintain our prioritized sustaining project list, and be the go-to person for program status, cost, and risk across our live Consumer products.

Key Responsibilities

- Sustaining Program Ownership: Own end-to-end program management for our live Consumer products, running the recurring Sustaining Core review and maintaining a tiered priority list spanning launch-risk, supply-stability, and cost-down workstreams.

- Engineering Change Management: Drive ECOs from proposal through approval, requalification, and production cutover, coordinating timing with contract manufacturers to avoid disruption to in-flight builds and inventory.

- Contract Manufacturer & Supply Chain Oversight: Hold overall program accountability for CM and supplier execution, partnering closely with the Head of Manufacturing and Head of Supply Chain, who own the direct supplier relationship and day-to-day execution.

- Finance Partnership: Serve as the point of contact for Finance on the accuracy of COGS projections and actuals, proactively flagging and reconciling variances so cost models and financial forecasts stay current.

- End-of-Life & Inventory Risk Management: Lead end-of-life planning and decisions for sustaining SKUs, including dead-stock and excess-and-obsolete (E&O) inventory risk analysis, to inform product transition timing and minimize financial exposure.

- Cost-Down Leadership: Lead cost-down and alternate-supply qualification initiatives (materials, suppliers, tooling) cross-functionally with Engineering, Product, Marketing, and other partners, sequencing work against business priority and driving from idea to implementation.

- Cross-Functional Alignment & Risk Management: Serve as the central point of contact and overall owner across engineering, quality, manufacturing, supply chain, and finance, proactively surfacing risks and ensuring the right operational leads are driving them to resolution.

- Executive Reporting: Deliver clear, regular updates on program health, budget, and risk to leadership via our Consumer program reviews.

Required Qualifications

- 5+ years of program or operations program management experience in hardware, consumer electronics, or appliances, including direct ownership of sustaining/post-launch programs.

- Proven experience managing contract manufacturers/EMS partners from mass production through end of life, including PO, pricing, and cost-variance management.

- Experience leading engineering change orders (ECOs) and coordinating their cross-functional approval and rollout.

- Strong cost and financial acumen, comfortable owning COGS tracking, budget variance, and cost-down initiatives.

- Excellent cross-functional communication skills, with experience running recurring program reviews and reporting program status to leadership.

- Ability to prioritize and sequence a broad portfolio of concurrent sustaining projects under resource constraints.

- Ability to travel domestically and internationally (including Mexico/Asia) to support build events as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

- Technical background in mechanical engineering, with familiarity with manufacturing processes such as metal stamping, injection molding, or tooling qualification.

- Spanish fluency and experience working with Mexico-based suppliers. Or Chinese fluency and experience with Asian suppliers.

- Experience with kitchen, thermal, or other consumer appliances.

Education & Experience

- BS degree desired (Engineering, Operations, or related field); MS or MBA a plus.

Why Join Us?

This is an opportunity to own a critical, highly visible function at a fast-growing hardware company — keeping our Consumer products running smoothly for the customers who already rely on them, while helping build the sustaining processes that will scale as our portfolio grows. If you thrive on solving cost, supply, and cross-functional puzzles in a fast-paced environment, we encourage you to apply.

The estimated base salary range for this position is $185k to $210k, which does not include the value of benefits or a potential equity grant. A wide range of factors are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets, market conditions, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and business and organizational needs. At Mill, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role.

jobs.title: Marketing Lead, Growth & Acquisition
jobs.description:
Mill is a waste prevention technology company reimagining what it means to eliminate waste, starting with food. We build smart systems and infrastructure for homes, businesses, and municipalities that transform food scraps from landfill-bound waste into valuable resources, including chicken feed. Tens of thousands of Mill’s residential food recyclers are already helping households divert millions of pounds of food scraps every year, paving the way for our upcoming launch of Mill Commercial—the industry’s first end-to-end solution for managing, understanding, and preventing food waste in commercial environments (e.g. grocery, restaurants, food services). At Mill, we are passionate about building easy-to-use, beautifully designed technologies that keep food in the food system and out of landfills.

The Context

Mill is at a pivotal point in our growth. We have found strong momentum in our Consumer business, and we are now focused on scaling household adoption of a new category that combines hardware, software, and service to change how people manage food waste.

At the same time, we are building toward a broader set of business lines. Alongside Consumer growth, we are developing commercial and institutional offerings that extend our impact through partners and enterprise environments. The two are complementary. Consumer establishes demand and habit, while Commercial expands reach and scale over time.

As we scale, we need to grow our acquisition engine with the same discipline we've brought to product. We are looking for a senior, hands-on growth marketer who can own paid and performance channels end to end — building an efficient, diversified, and continuously improving customer acquisition engine that serves both consumer and commercial buyers.

This role reports to the GM of Consumer and works closely with Growth, Analytics, Creative, Sales, and Business Operations.

The Mandate

This person owns Mill's customer acquisition engine — the paid channels, performance metrics, and testing infrastructure that turn marketing spend into efficient, scalable growth across our consumer and commercial business lines. The remit is both strategic and deeply operational:

- Own the paid acquisition engine. Own the paid acquisition engine. Manage strategy, budget, and day-to-day execution across paid social, paid search, programmatic/display, affiliate, and marketplace channels.

- Drive full-funnel growth. Drive full-funnel growth. Own the media mix and budget allocation across channels, set bidding and pacing strategy, and continuously reallocate spend toward the highest-efficiency opportunities.

- Build rigorous measurement and experimentation. Build rigorous measurement and experimentation. Own attribution, CAC/LTV modeling, and incrementality testing; run a disciplined test-and-learn program across audiences, offers, and channels.

- Partner on high-performing creative. Partner on high-performing creative. Brief Creative and agency partners on what's working in-market, and run a rapid creative-testing cadence to keep performance improving.

- Optimize the conversion funnel. Optimize the conversion funnel. Partner with Product and Growth on landing pages, checkout flow, and onboarding to lift conversion rate and improve payback period.

- Build the commercial acquisition motion. Build the commercial acquisition motion. Partner with Sales and Business Operations to build paid lead-generation and co-marketing programs that fill the pipeline for partner and enterprise buyers.

- Operate with rigor. Operate with rigor. Own CAC, ROAS, and payback targets, manage budget and pacing across channels, and report performance with clarity to leadership.

- Turn data into advantage. Turn data into advantage. Partner with Analytics and Data Science to understand what's driving (and limiting) efficient growth, and translate that insight into targeting, channel, and creative decisions.

- Apply learnings forward. Apply learnings forward. Build Mill's growth playbook so each channel, cohort, and campaign compounds on the last.

Success in 12 to 18 Months Looks Like

- Mill runs an efficient, diversified paid acquisition engine that hits CAC and payback targets across consumer and commercial buyers.

- A rigorous test-and-learn culture is in place, with a clear experimentation roadmap and reliable read on incrementality.

- Channel mix is diversified enough to reduce dependency risk on any single platform.

- Commercial and partner lead-generation has a repeatable engine that reliably fills the sales pipeline.

- The growth playbook is documented and portable across new channels, markets, and business lines.

- This person is a trusted thought partner to the GM of Consumer and to cross-functional leaders, shaping decisions beyond marketing alone.

Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate brings:

- 8 to 12+ years of marketing experience, with deep, hands-on expertise in growth or performance marketing across paid social, paid search, and programmatic channels.

- A track record of building efficient, scalable acquisition engines for new products or categories, with demonstrated command of CAC, LTV, and payback economics.

- Experience owning a paid media budget and performance targets, with the operational rigor to manage pacing, bidding, and ROI in real time.

- Fluency with attribution, analytics, and experimentation — comfortable designing and reading incrementality tests, not just dashboards.

- Fluency partnering with Creative, Analytics, Data Science, and external agency and media partners to ship and iterate on high-performing campaigns.

- Comfort operating in ambiguity, moving from strategy to execution without waiting for perfect information.

- Strong resonance with Mill's mission and values, and a belief that growth and impact are mutually reinforcing.

- Fluency in common collaboration, analytics, and project management tools (Google Suite, Excel, Notion / Coda, and paid media/analytics platforms).

Operating Attributes

Attribute

Description

Growth Operator

Builds and runs an efficient, scalable paid acquisition engine from the ground up.

Channel Expert

Deep, hands-on fluency across paid social, paid search, and programmatic; knows how to get the most out of each platform.

Data-Driven

Uses CAC/LTV, attribution, and incrementality testing to prioritize spend, without losing customer empathy.

Rigorous Experimenter

Runs a disciplined test-and-learn cadence across creative, audiences, and channels.

Cross-Functional Partner

Collaborates deeply with Growth, Creative, Analytics, Sales, and Operations to deliver integrated results.

Mission-Driven

Brings authentic belief in climate impact and sustainability as a growth advantage, not a constraint.

Compensation

The estimated base salary range for this position is $205k - $235k, which does not include the value of benefits or a potential equity grant. A wide range of factors are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to skill sets, market conditions, experience and training, and business and organizational needs. At Mill, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their role.

jobs.title: Senior Integrated Marketing Manager (Contract)
jobs.description:
Mill is a waste prevention technology company reimagining what it means to eliminate waste, starting with food. We build smart systems and infrastructure for homes, businesses, and municipalities that transform food scraps from landfill-bound waste into valuable resources, including chicken feed. Tens of thousands of Mill’s residential food recyclers are already helping households divert millions of pounds of food scraps every year, paving the way for our upcoming launch of Mill Commercial—the industry’s first end-to-end solution for managing, understanding, and preventing food waste in commercial environments (e.g. grocery, restaurants, food services). At Mill, we are passionate about building easy-to-use, beautifully designed technologies that keep food in the food system and out of landfills.

The Role

This is a contract Marketing Manager role covering three concurrent workstreams: Mill's first national retail pilot, holiday campaign execution, and marketing partnerships. To be successful in this role, you'll manage complex cross-functional programs, build clear creative and strategic briefs, bring a working knowledge of the retail landscape and negotiate and manage partnerships.

Key Responsibilities

1. Retail Pilot Program Management

- Serve as the connective tissue between Mill and the retailer's merchant/buyer team on marketing workstreams (distinct from the sales/BD relationship).

- Continue executing program marketing in support of pilot and holiday.

- Lead Assisted Selling and Store Engagement programs, training and supporting staff and translating learnings to other workstreams.

- Plan and manage paid media on the retailer's own ad platform, and report on performance.

2. Holiday Campaign Management

- Support holiday campaign execution from Cyber Week through New Year's Eve.

- Partner with channel leads (paid, social, email, product) to ensure creative deliverables are completed and campaign is launched seamlessly.

- Keep the campaign on track and on budget, managing stakeholders to timely delivery.

3. Partnerships

- Manage and help execute partnerships, including commitments with our existing community of Influencers, brand partnerships and community partners.

Who You Are

- A Retail Marketing Operator: You've run physical in-store activation before, including display/POS production and navigating retailer merchandising constraints.

- Comfortable in Ambiguity: You build process while executing against fixed external deadlines, and don't need a complete playbook to start.

- A Data-Backed Storyteller: You can report on the details and understand the story for an exec audience.

- A Cross-Functional Operator: You coordinate programs across diverse teams.

- AI-enabled Approach: You err on the side of applying AI to help scale your workflows with increasing speed and efficiency.

Qualifications & Requirements

- 10+ years in marketing, with direct experience in retail, channel, or shopper marketing.

- Has managed retail media campaigns on at least one major platform (Amazon Ads, Walmart Connect, Target Roundel, Instacart Ads, or similar).

- Has managed external agency/vendor relationships and can write a clear creative or production brief.

- Partnership or influencer marketing experience, from sourcing through measurement.

- A plus, not a requirement: experience with a new-to-market or new-category product.

Details

- Contract Duration: 6+ months

- Location: San Bruno, CA (in-office most days)

- Commitment: Full-time contractor

- Reports to: GM, Consumer
